title: Risotto al Radicchio
subtitle: Venetian bitter radicchio risotto with red wine
excerpt: Risotto al radicchio is a Venetian dish with a distinctly bitter, wine-dark character. Radicchio is wilted in butter, red wine is added, and the rice cooks in a deep garnet stock until glossy and pink-tinged. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Risotto al radicchio is a classic of Venetian cooking, drawing on the bitter radicchio varieties cultivated in the Veneto since the 16th century. Radicchio di Treviso (the long, tapered variety with white ribs and deep red leaves) is the traditional choice; radicchio di Chioggia (the compact round variety) is more widely available. Both work, though Treviso is more dramatic in colour and slightly more bitter. The use of red wine in the risotto base is specific to this dish: it contributes to the characteristic pink-red colour of the finished risotto and adds a subtle tartness that balances the bitterness of the radicchio.

glossaryTerms.definition: A bitter Italian chicory with dark red or purple leaves and white ribs. Radicchio di Treviso (tapered, elongated head) and radicchio di Chioggia (compact round head) are the two common varieties. Both are bitter when raw; cooking sweetens them considerably while preserving a residual bitterness that defines this risotto.

content.text: looks as unusual as it tastes: the finished dish is a deep pink-red, stained by the radicchio and wine. The flavour is bitter and sweet at once, the bitterness of the wilted radicchio softened by the butter mantecatura and the Parmesan but never eliminated. It is a distinctly Venetian character.

Reserve a few radicchio leaves to add raw at the end. Their bright colour and slight crunch contrast with the soft risotto. The rest is wilted in butter before the rice is added, which concentrates the flavour and contributes the pink colour to the stock.

items.prepNote: one large head, shredded, a few leaves reserved

content.text: Melt half the {{unsalted-butter}} of butter with {{olive-oil}} of olive oil in a wide heavy pan over a medium heat. Add {{onion}} of onion and cook for 8 minutes until soft. Add {{garlic}} of garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add the shredded {{radicchio}} of radicchio (reserving a few leaves for serving) and stir for 3 to 4 minutes until wilted and collapsed. Add {{arborio-rice}} of rice and toast for 1 minute.

Add {{red-wine}} of red wine and stir until absorbed. Begin adding {{stock-vegetable}} of hot vegetable stock a ladle at a time, stirring constantly and waiting for each addition to absorb before adding the next. This takes 18 to 20 minutes. The risotto will turn deep pink as it cooks.

When the rice has slight bite but is cooked through, remove from the heat. Add the remaining cold butter and {{parmesan}} of Parmesan and beat vigorously for 2 minutes. Season. Rest 1 minute and serve topped with the reserved raw radicchio.

items.symptom: Risotto colour is muddy rather than pink-red
items.cause: Radicchio not wilted properly before stock added, or white wine used instead of red
items.fix: Wilt the radicchio fully before adding the rice. Red wine is essential to the colour.

items.cause: Radicchio di Treviso is more bitter than di Chioggia; or not enough mantecatura butter
items.fix: Use di Chioggia (round head) for a milder result. A generous mantecatura of cold butter balances bitterness effectively.

content.text: Radicchio belongs to the Veneto more than anywhere else. The area around Treviso has grown it since the 16th century. Risotto al radicchio is a winter dish in Venice and the Veneto, on menus from October to February. The deep pink colour is striking. The flavour is bitter, warming, and quite unlike any other risotto.
